scope: Final gate review of existing Americas and Oceania local-food, irrigation, raised-field and island records for promotion to two-sided Malthusian capacity anchors.

review_summary.disposition: No reviewed record has all of a defensible two-sided population or capacity interval, independent saturation/pressure evidence, predominantly local food, and an EU5-mappable boundary with at least 95 percent coverage. Existing one-sided and validation records remain available for diagnostics only.

records.label: Hohokam Lower Salt River/Phoenix Basin irrigated communities
records.population_interval_status: broad archaeological settlement-proxy interval; not a census and not coextensive with the capacity footprint
records.capacity_interval_status: Piman-analogy and agricultural scenario reconstruction; one-sided physical constraint only

local_food_evidence.food_regime: canal-irrigated maize, beans, squash and local riverine foods

pressure_evidence: Lower Salt canals and fields were exposed to low-flow drought, floods and salt-laden water.
Archaeological evidence records agricultural intensification and later depopulation around the fifteenth century.

The Marana/Piman comparison estimates about 2,300-5,800 people per 1,000 irrigated hectares and extrapolates 53,000-133,000 for the Phoenix system; this is an analogy-derived potential, not observed equilibrium.
rejection_reasons: The population packet uses a broad regional archaeological range, while the 53,000-133,000 capacity envelope is a model/ethnographic analogy; they are not an independent two-sided observation.

The population crosswalk is an approximate akimel_oodham province selector with about 0.60 coverage, whereas the capacity lower-bound crosswalk contains only two broad EU5 locations (guwevkabaya and yavpe) and compares 210 km2 of reconstructed irrigated corridor with an 18,731 km2 EU5 footprint.

Salinity, drought, flood and abandonment establish production pressure but do not identify a dated saturation fraction. Preserve the vetted 53,000-person one-sided constraint; do not promote it to a global scale anchor.
records.boundary_status: historical irrigated corridor is not coextensive with whole EU5 cells
records.notes: Independent salinity and hydrology studies make this a valuable physical stress case, but not an independent upper label.

records.label: Upper Mantaro Wanka II settlement system
records.population_interval_status: lower bound only; no defensible upper interval or saturation fraction

local_food_evidence.food_regime: highland potatoes, maize, tubers, camelids and local agricultural production

pressure_evidence: UMARP/JASP settlement survey documents dense provincial settlement and agricultural intensification.
Defensive settlement, warfare and post-conquest reorganization create unresolved migration and shock effects.
The 61,000 figure is a conservative lower bound for the northern Upper Mantaro system, not a saturation observation.
rejection_reasons: No independent capacity interval or literature-supported saturation fraction is supplied; a lower bound cannot establish the model scale.
The 1,900 km2 research umbrella is represented by a six-location Hatun Xauxa selector covering about 11,046.6 km2, so a whole-cell target would silently add unobserved land.
Warfare, Inca conquest and settlement relocation prevent interpreting the observed lower bound as a stable Malthusian equilibrium.
records.boundary_status: high-containment broad selector; only one-sided scoring allowed
records.notes: Retain the 61,000-person lower bound for one-sided validation; do not invent an upper interval.

records.label: Mesa Verde Village Ecodynamics Project phase-I landscape
records.population_interval_status: modelled settlement population point used as a one-sided constraint
records.capacity_interval_status: not an independently observed capacity interval

local_food_evidence.food_regime: predominantly local dry-farmed maize, beans, squash and gathered foods

pressure_evidence: Village Ecodynamics work identifies drought, soil/resource stress and unused maize potential before regional abandonment.
The 19,404 estimate is a reconstructed settlement total, not a census with a dated equilibrium interval.
rejection_reasons: The 1,800 km2 study polygon is contained by one EU5 location of about 9,104.1 km2; the historical footprint is only about 19.8 percent of the cell. Whole-cell extrapolation is not permitted.
The observed population and environmental stress do not define a saturation fraction; departure and migration are unresolved.
The VEP estimate can test drought, soil and protein constraints and remains a one-sided lower bound, but cannot supervise a two-sided scale.
records.boundary_status: high containment but non-coextensive study polygon
records.notes: Use as a hostile/drought validation case and lower bound only.

records.label: Tongatapu local-food population and capacity reconstructions
records.population_interval_status: two incompatible reconstructions; no reconciled interval
records.capacity_interval_status: Green/Ussher scenario envelope, not independent saturation evidence

local_food_evidence.food_regime: yam, taro, sweet potato, banana, breadfruit, coconut, fishing and livestock

pressure_evidence: Archaeobotanical work documents primary-forest removal, intensive multicropping and bush-fallow pressure.
Independent LiDAR study reports a substantially larger population range than the Green/Ussher reconstruction.
rejection_reasons: The 18,000-24,000 envelope is derived from the same Green/Ussher modelling family as the lower-bound packet and cannot serve as an independent upper label.
The independent 50,000-60,000 estimate conflicts by roughly a factor of three; the conflict is unresolved and cannot be hidden in a narrow uncertainty interval.
The exact island crosswalk is excellent (0.976 area coverage), but mapping quality cannot repair unresolved source semantics and saturation evidence.
records.boundary_status: near-exact island mapping; evidence conflict unresolved
records.notes: Preserve the existing local-food lower bound and use the disagreement as a validation/uncertainty diagnostic.

records.label: Mangareva pre-contact food-system capacity scenarios
records.population_interval_status: no independent historical population interval for the same boundary

local_food_evidence.food_regime: terraced/horticultural island foods, arboriculture, marine and lagoon resources

pressure_evidence: Puleston et al. model resource and labour constraints under alternative pre-contact food-system scenarios.
No independent dated land-scarcity or famine evidence establishes that the upper scenario was approached.
rejection_reasons: There is no independent population or saturation interval; the only quantitative interval is a modelled food-capacity scenario.
The semantic EU5 tag is exact, but the tag footprint is about 525.6 km2 while the published Mangareva land area is 16.58 km2 (roughly 31.7 times smaller).
A coarse-cell capacity cannot be treated as an island target without resolving the area mismatch.
records.boundary_status: semantic island tag but non-coextensive EU5 footprint
records.notes: Keep as an out-of-period/food-system validation envelope, not a scale anchor.

records.label: Tiwanaku Lake Titicaca raised-field sustaining-area reconstruction
records.population_interval_status: no independent population interval for the mapped raised-field area

local_food_evidence.food_regime: raised-field potatoes, quinoa, tubers, camelids and lake resources

pressure_evidence: Raised-field experiments and palaeoecology provide strong physical evidence for frost-buffered agricultural productivity.
Kolata explicitly notes that historical Tiwanaku population did not approach the calculated ecological ceiling.
rejection_reasons: The 285,000-1,111,500 range is a physical potential, not an observed Malthusian equilibrium or independent saturation interval.
The raised-field evidence covers about 190 km2 while the seven-location EU5 province selector covers about 15,410 km2; whole-cell extrapolation would add unobserved land.
No two-sided target can be formed from population estimates and a model-derived ceiling alone.
records.boundary_status: high-containment broad province; raised-field footprint is a small subset
records.notes: Use for crop-water, frost and raised-field physical validation only.

records.label: Classic Maya lowlands LiDAR settlement system
records.population_interval_status: regional demographic reconstruction outside the target date; no saturation interval

local_food_evidence.food_regime: maize, beans, squash, manioc and managed wetlands/forest foods

pressure_evidence: LiDAR settlement density and land-use studies document intensive agriculture and late Classic stress.
Political collapse, warfare and migration confound any interpretation as a stable Malthusian ceiling.
rejection_reasons: The date is substantially earlier than 1337 and the source provides no independent saturation fraction.
The mapped study region has only about 0.86 EU5 coverage and contains heterogeneous karst, wetland and upland systems.
The broad population interval cannot supervise intrinsic capacity without resolving urban, political and migration components.
records.notes: Retain as a held-out intensive-landscape validation analogue.

records.label: Casarabe Llanos de Mojos managed-landscape settlement system
records.population_interval_status: broad archaeological scenario range; no independent saturation interval

local_food_evidence.food_regime: raised fields, forest management, fish and seasonally wetland agriculture

pressure_evidence: Earthworks, causeways and raised fields demonstrate durable local food investment.
The evidence does not establish that any dated population interval was at a long-run ceiling.
rejection_reasons: The current EU5 crosswalk covers only about 0.20 of the proposed Moxos selector, below the 95 percent quantitative threshold.
The population range is broad and scenario-based, with no independent pressure-to-saturation interval.
The date range crosses multiple settlement phases and cannot be treated as a single equilibrium target.
records.notes: Use as a managed-landscape physical validation case; no training label.

records.label: Upper Xingu pre-contact managed landscape
records.population_interval_status: broad scenario estimate; no dated local-food saturation interval

local_food_evidence.food_regime: manioc, maize, fish, agroforestry and managed soil/forest systems

pressure_evidence: Archaeological and ethnohistoric work documents dense villages, roads, fish management and anthropogenic soils.
The cited range does not demonstrate that the system reached a Malthusian equilibrium, and later contact shocks are substantial.
rejection_reasons: No independent capacity or saturation interval is available for a mappable rural boundary.
The population estimate spans an order of magnitude and is not tied to a single dated settlement footprint.
The region is not currently crosswalked to EU5 with the required 95 percent coverage.
records.notes: Retain for held-out managed-forest and fisheries validation, not scale fitting.
